rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest to punitive: L33 'The designer points at the line in the output that went generic' and L67 'A polished technical plan beside a people plan full of UNASSIGNED is a finding'. Both are about the file/plan, not the person, and the unease is not-knowing ('Monday's questions'); L79 'The old way stayed because it did the job well enough' protects the team from blame. Student leaves uncertain about what travels, not ashamed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Lead with discipline, not failure mode.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest to failure-led: L73 'and how the switch would fail' and the failure story in the phase-5 fence. The discipline leads (H1 'Take it to the team', 'Test the switch', way of working as a proposal); the failure story is the negative case the test addresses, one story, not the title.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strategy-fidelity check.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Facets checked. Front-run: the body asks 'what would have to be true for your wider team to switch' (L73) before the lecture slide 'What would have to be true for your team to switch?' names it; maintainer L105 records that as deliberate (Martin left unnamed), exercise-then-name order. Phase 2 does not name 'an agent's instructions are not the agent' (grep 'not the agent' on body = 0). Big Idea ('What is each of us for ...'): roles are distinct in the body (PO takes outcome questions L39, designer the job in team's words, PO says which assumption sinks it L77, each gives own Monday move in the apt101-d3-team-monday fence (L89)). Arc: closes on L91 'It is a proposal. The team that lives with it decides.' which hands to Sharpen the proposal and repeats, in a different dose, the lecture closer 'On Monday the team decides' (a model repeated, not a spent reveal, check_pedagogy 9b). Mood does not resolve early: no verification step closes the unease; the proposal stays open. Closest to violating: L91, as above.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Group beat ≠ parallel solo work.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Remove the room test: three people share one driver (L11 'The team lead drives'), one frame and one team/monday.md; with the room removed the Way of working frame and the merged proposal do not exist. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The room's output is named as an artefact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Group output named: maintainer L110 'Way of working frame (board, the call and the sentence at its head)' and 'team/monday.md'; individual output named beside it: each role's Monday move (fence at L89). Both registers present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: React, don't author.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest to blank-page authoring: L19 three columns of post-its. They start from material to correct: 'The team lead starts from the draft made on Day 2; the designer and the product owner add what the five users showed you' (L19). Phase 2 reacts to a stranger's file; phases 3-5 Claude drafts and the trio corrects ('Read module-7/jtbd.md ... point at the generic line').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Pre-built material is a hard prerequisite, stated in the module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prerequisite stated: module Meta 'Paired trios: ... the trainer pairs them before the day' and 'the trainer sets up three frames on each team's Miro board before the day'; exercise maintainer L115 'Room: phase 2 needs trios paired before the day'. Degradation named: 'without it, a frame screenshot into the chat and the team lead posts the proposal by hand'. Closest: the degradation for an unpaired trio is not named (see suggestion at L115).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Attribution is stated by a human, recorded verbatim.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: the L89 fence 'Ask each of us in turn for our first Monday move' and 'with our names': the human states own move and name, Claude records; nothing is inferred from a transcript. Attribution stated by a human.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Nothing is written over.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The L89 fence posts the proposal 'inside it, beside our post-its', so earlier post-its are not overwritten; phase 1 adds post-its 'at the head' of the frame without removing. Closest: the room is not told in so many words that disagreement is kept; the beat is a trio proposing, not an adjudication of competing claims, so the hedging harm is absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Filing is invisible.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Participants steer and react; Claude files. Closest: L23 'sends one file across' and L87 'opens team/what-goes-in.md', which are the beat's content (hand-over, door), not participants naming or formatting records; phase 3-6 files are written by Claude to fixed module-7/ paths.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Scope-of-sharing is declared before contribution, not after.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Scope declared before contribution: L23 'sends one file across, and only that file' names what leaves the trio before it does; L87-L89 puts the door ('which sources its agents may read, what stays out, and that anyone may say no') as the first line of the proposal. Closest: no tier language for the post-its, which stay inside the trio's own frame.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A decision beat needs a real constraint.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Constraints supplied: L48 and the fence 'Let us pick one to three'; L77 'The product owner says which one would sink the proposal if it is false'; the L75 fence lists five assumptions 'Most load-bearing first' then two or three tested. Not a polite-consensus pick.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Group decisions are human, and named as such.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L77 'the three of you choose'; L48 'When Claude asks you to pick, pick'. Claude lists and writes; the trio decides, and the wider team decides after (L91). No voting or auto-promotion.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Protected beat decided in advance: module Meta 'Protected: five users phase 4 ... and take it to the team phase 6 (team/monday.md). Overrun: ...'. This exercise's protected phase is 6.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No mechanical coverage — the trainer guide carries the load.
